text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall — high error rate observed when fetching model artifacts from Hugging Face (hf.co). Root cause suspected HF hosting rate limits. See alert: https://internal.ops/alerts/ARTIFACT_FETCH_HIGH_ERR

jamie: I’m on it. seeing 429s in the fetch logs across multiple regions. cold-starts are spiking.

sara: can you paste the log snippet? are these 429s from hf-hosting or our CDN?

jamie: logs: ```2026-03-15T13:46:02Z fetcher[pool-3] WARN fetch_model: url=https://hf.co/models/rdwdl/large/weights.tar status=429 retry_after=3s``` repeated ~2k/sec across us-east-1 and eu-west-1.

rohan: confirmed same in staging mirror metrics. looks like HF returning backoff headers intermittently. 429s correlate with a surge after yesterday's traffic shift.

maria: any customer impact yet?

jamie: yes — ~8% of hosted inference requests are failing to initialize due to missing model artifact on cold start. Warm in-flight requests are fine. Affected customers: a few PLG trial orgs and 1 mid-market customer (acme-corp) hitting spikes.

oncall-sre: Triage plan: 1) enable aggressive local prefetch on Dedicated and Hosted where safe 2) fall back to cached quantized variant for affected routes 3) widen artifact mirror pool 4) contact HF support and enable mirror serving. I'll coordinate.

sara: How do we enable prefetch quickly? Is there a runbook?

rohan: we have a self-serve flag: `ENABLE_PREFETCH=true` per deployment. For hosted, we can flip a global feature flag. For Dedicated, we patch the node-agent config. Quick command: ```curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"enable_prefetch":true, "prefetch_threads":4}' https://console.internal/api/feature-flags/prefetch```

jamie: I can flip hosted now, but want to limit rate to avoid thundering prefetch. Will set prefetch_ratelimit=5/sec per model.

maria: Good call. Also we should enable fallback to our smaller quantized variant: change model routing to `rdwdl/large:q4` when fetch fails > 3 times. Can we do that as a policy?

rohan: yes — add a route policy with `fallback_variants` in routing cfg. Example patch: ```route: /v1/generate model: rdwdl/large fallback: [rdwdl/large-q4, rdwdl/medium] backoff: 3``` I’ll queue a canary.

oncall-sre: Metrics tasks: jamie, add a dashboard showing artifact 429 rate, cold-start latency, and number of fallback activations. Put an alarm if fallback > 2% of traffic for > 5m.

jamie: added quick dashboard and alert (link: https://dash.internal/d/ARTIFACT_FETCH). pushing prefetch flag now.

incident-bot: deploy-bot reports: Hosted feature flag ENABLE_PREFETCH set -> successful across 6 control plane regions.

sara: I’m seeing immediate drop in cold-start errors in eu-west-1 — 429s still at HF but our prefetch is catching some artifacts from mirrors.

maria: Reached out to HF support with case #HF-2026-347. Mentioned rate-limit patterns and asked for temporary quota bump and mirror enablement.

rohan: in parallel, I’m adding more mirrors to the artifact-registry config. That will allow us to serve from internal points when HF is slow. Patch applied to mirror list and rolling restart of fetcher service in progress.

jamie: FYI we found a bad interaction: our prefetch logic was retrying aggressively on 429 without honoring `retry-after`. I pushed a quick fix to respect retry-after and exponential backoff. Patch: ```diff --git a/fetcher b/fetcher + respect_retry_after = true + backoff_base = 2s```

oncall-sre: Nice find. That would have just amplified HF throttling. Good call on the ratelimit.

incident-bot: automatic page update: oncall-sre has appeared.

oncall-sre: I'm taking lead. Current mitigation state: PREFETCH=ON (hosted), fallback routing enabled (q4), fetcher respects retry-after, mirrors extended. HF case open. Customer impact: degraded cold-start success rate earlier, now improving. Action items assigned.

maria: Can we notify the affected customers with an incident banner and temporary workaround? Support, please draft a message that says we are experiencing upstream artifact hosting rate limits; we have mitigations and no data loss, recommend trying again for failed requests.

jamie: I'll post a status note to status.redwood.ai: "Investigating artifact fetch failures from Hugging Face causing cold-start issues; mitigations in progress."

sara: perf note: prefetch is adding small cost (bandwidth) but reduces 99p cold-start latency by 60%. overall positive.

rohan: timeline so far: 13:46 alert -> 13:52 prefetch flag -> 13:58 fallback routing -> 14:03 fetcher backoff fix -> 14:10 mirrors extended -> 14:15 HF acknowledged case.

oncall-sre: Next: keep monitoring for 60m. If HF doesn't restore limits, schedule larger mirror provisioning and consider temporary throttling of new cold-starts for non-paying tiers to preserve capacity for enterprise customers.

maria: noted, will coordinate comms.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident status changed to mitigated (partial). Please update ticket with postmortem follow-ups.

jamie: Postmortem items I’ll own: 1) make prefetch default with safe rate-limits 2) add unit test for honoring retry-after 3) automations to trigger mirror expansion on 429 spike.

rohan: I’ll own routing fallback rollout docs and add a canary gate.

sara: I’ll help with customer impact list and support messages.

maria: Thanks team. I’ll keep HF support engaged and escalate if quota bump not granted within 2h. If we need to, we’ll cut a temporary downgrade policy for free tiers.

oncall-sre: Closing bridge for now — we'll reopen if alerts return above threshold. Great quick coordination. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Bridge closed by oncall-sre.
